Full tables, accurate menus and a daily close you can trust

For dine-in restaurants, QSR chains and multi-brand cloud kitchens, we connect the POS, aggregator integrations and WhatsApp so bookings and waitlists run from one book, sold-out dishes come off every channel, ratings are watched by item and outlet, and owners get a reliable morning report.

The challenge

What makes restaurants & cloud kitchens different.

01

Bookings arrive by phone, DMs and apps, so the host stand works from partial lists and no-shows hit peak nights.

02

Dishes that run out stay live on aggregators, causing cancellations and falling ratings.

03

Aggregator payouts arrive net of commission, ads and penalties, and differences are hard to trace back to orders.

04

Wastage and stock variance stay invisible until food cost looks wrong at month end.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for restaurants & cloud kitchens.

01

One reservation book and a fair waitlist

Bookings from WhatsApp, Instagram, Google and the website in one place, same-day confirmations, and table-ready messages for walk-in guests.

02

Stock-linked menu switch-offs

Low stock on a key ingredient lists the affected items across brands; the outlet manager confirms, and the POS or integration partner switches them off on Swiggy, Zomato and other channels.

03

Ratings and complaints by dish and outlet

A daily digest that groups ratings, complaints and cancellation reasons by dish, brand, outlet and shift, with tasks raised for repeat issues such as packaging or late handover.

04

Morning close for owners

Sales by channel and brand, wastage, stock variance and aggregator settlement exceptions in a one-page summary, with aggregator sales reported separately for GST.

05

Service recovery and loyalty

Private feedback after a visit or delivered order, recovery cases for low scores, and consented offers for regulars and lapsed guests.

Discover and inquireStandard3–5 weeks

Aggregator menu sync and rating watch

Keep Swiggy, Zomato and other ordering channels in step with what the kitchen can actually make, and give each brand and outlet a daily digest of ratings, complaints and the dishes behind them.

Restaurants & cloud kitchens

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

When a dish runs out but stays live on aggregators, orders get canceled or substituted and ratings fall. Cloud kitchens running several brands from one kitchen feel this most. Ratings and complaints sit in separate partner dashboards, so patterns by dish, outlet or shift are spotted late.

Trigger

A stock-out or low-stock signal from the POS or inventory module, a scheduled availability check before each service, and the daily ratings export.

How it runs

  • Map every aggregator item and add-on to its POS item and recipe, across brands and outlets.
  • When stock of a key ingredient falls below its set level, list the affected items for each brand and ask the outlet manager to confirm the switch-off on WhatsApp or Slack.
  • Switch confirmed items off through the POS or aggregator integration partner, such as Petpooja or UrbanPiper, and back on when stock is received.
  • Compare live aggregator availability against the POS before each service and alert on items that are live but out of stock.
  • Ingest ratings, complaints and cancellation reasons from partner exports, group them by dish, brand, outlet and issue type, and send a daily digest.
  • Raise a task for repeated issues, such as late handover, packaging or portion complaints, to the kitchen or operations owner.

Human checkpoint

The outlet manager confirms switch-offs for items outside a pre-approved list and owns every response to complaints. Food safety complaints go straight to the outlet's food safety supervisor and are never closed by automation.

  • Aggregator integration partner (for example UrbanPiper)

How we measure it

  • Rating trend by brand and outlet
  • Repeat complaint themes closed

Quote, confirm and payStarter2–4 weeks

Table reservations, reminders and waitlist

Take bookings from Google, Instagram, WhatsApp and the website into one book, confirm and remind guests on the day, run a fair walk-in waitlist with table-ready messages, and record no-shows for next time.

Restaurants & cloud kitchens

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Bookings come through calls, DMs and several apps, so the host stand works from partial lists. No-shows on busy nights cost covers, walk-in guests leave when the queue is unclear, and nobody knows which guests repeatedly cancel late or which are regulars.

Trigger

A booking request from any connected channel, a scheduled reminder before service, or a walk-in guest added to the waitlist at the host stand.

How it runs

  • Collect bookings from WhatsApp, Instagram messages, the website form and reservation partners into one book with party size, time, occasion and seating notes.
  • Check capacity rules by table mix and shift, confirm the booking with an approved utility template, and offer alternative times when the slot is full.
  • Send a same-day reminder asking guests to confirm or cancel with one tap, and release canceled tables to the waitlist.
  • Add walk-ins to a digital waitlist from a tablet at the host stand, quote a realistic wait from current table turns, and message guests when their table is ready.
  • Record arrivals, no-shows and late cancellations, and tag regulars and occasions so the host sees them on the next visit.

Human checkpoint

The host or floor manager decides seating, overbooking on peak nights and any deposit or cancellation charge. Deposit and cancellation policies are written by the owner and shown to guests before they book.

Stay, dine, travel or celebrateStandard4–6 weeks

Outlet daily close: sales, settlements and wastage

Each morning, combine POS sales, aggregator orders and payouts, stock counts and wastage logs into one report per outlet and brand, with exceptions flagged for the owner and the accounts team.

Restaurants & cloud kitchens

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Owners piece together yesterday's numbers from the POS, two or three aggregator dashboards, payment apps and a kitchen notebook. Aggregator payouts arrive net of commission, ads and penalties, and differences are found months later. Wastage and stock variance stay invisible until food cost looks wrong at month end.

Trigger

A scheduled run after the last service closes, plus a weekly run when aggregator settlement statements arrive.

How it runs

  • Pull day-end sales by channel, brand and item from the POS, and order data from aggregator exports or the integration partner.
  • Record wastage and closing stock for key items through a short staff form at close, with a photo for high-value waste.
  • Compare theoretical consumption from recipes with actual stock movement and flag variances beyond an agreed tolerance.
  • Match aggregator settlement statements to orders, separating commission, ad spend, penalties and taxes, and list unexplained differences.
  • Report aggregator orders separately from direct sales, because the aggregator pays GST on restaurant services ordered through it, and share the file with the accountant.
  • Send the owner a one-page morning summary by WhatsApp or email, with drill-down in the dashboard.

Human checkpoint

The outlet manager confirms wastage entries and explains variances. The accountant reviews settlement differences and GST reporting before filing and raises disputes with aggregators.

Feedback and recoveryStandard3–5 weeks

Feedback, service recovery and review replies

Ask every guest for private feedback after a stay, meal, trip or event, open a recovery case when something went wrong, invite every guest to review without filtering, and draft replies to public reviews for a manager to approve.

Hotels & resorts · Restaurants & cloud kitchens · Travel agencies & tour operators · Event & wedding venues

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Unhappy guests often say nothing until they post a review, and happy guests rarely write one unless asked. Replies to Google, OTA and aggregator reviews are slow or generic, and some businesses ask only satisfied guests for reviews, which Google's review policies prohibit.

Trigger

Checkout in the PMS, a closed bill or delivered order, a trip's return date or the day after an event, plus each new public review on a connected platform.

How it runs

  • Send a short private feedback request through an approved template or email, timed for each segment.
  • Open a recovery case for low scores or complaint keywords, assigned to the guest relations, outlet, consultant or event manager with a response target.
  • Send every eligible guest the same review invitation regardless of their feedback score, with no incentive attached.
  • Collect new public reviews from Google Business Profile and other connected sources, and classify sentiment, topics and any serious allegation.
  • Draft a specific, courteous reply in the brand voice from the review and approved facts, and route serious allegations such as food safety, discrimination or injury to the general manager.
  • Post the approved reply through the Google Business Profile API where connected, or give the approver a copy-ready reply for the OTA or aggregator extranet.

Human checkpoint

A named manager edits and approves every public reply and decides every refund, compensation or goodwill gesture. Allegations involving safety, health, discrimination or legal threats go to the general manager or owner before any response.

Return and referStandard4–6 weeks

Repeat guest, loyalty and win-back program

Use visit and booking history to recognize regulars, send consented offers on occasions that matter to each guest, invite lapsed guests back, and remind sales ahead of corporate clients' annual events.

Restaurants & cloud kitchens · Travel agencies & tour operators · Event & wedding venues

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Most hospitality businesses hold years of guest data in POS, booking and CRM systems but rarely use it. Regulars are not recognized, birthdays and anniversaries pass unnoticed, and repeat corporate events go to competitors because nobody called in time. Mass promotions that ignore consent damage trust and break messaging rules.

Trigger

Scheduled segment updates from POS, booking and CRM data, plus date-based triggers such as birthdays, anniversaries, trip anniversaries and the anniversary of a corporate event.

How it runs

  • Build a single guest profile from POS, booking and CRM records with visit frequency, spend band, preferences and consent status per channel.
  • Define segments with the marketing owner, such as regulars, lapsed guests, occasion dates, repeat travelers by destination interest and corporate event clients.
  • Send approved marketing templates or emails only to guests with marketing opt-in, with an opt-out in every message and frequency caps.
  • Track visit-based rewards in the POS loyalty module for restaurants, suggest trips from past destinations for travel, and alert venue sales managers ahead of a client's annual event date.
  • Measure returns, bookings and opt-outs per campaign against a holdout group, and retire offers that do not bring guests back.

Human checkpoint

The marketing owner approves segments, offers and every template. The sales manager decides and makes outreach to corporate and event clients personally. Discounts beyond agreed limits need owner approval.

Tools

Systems it connects

  • Travel CRM
  • Event CRM or banquet system
  • Messaging and email consent records

Data & consent

Marketing consent is recorded separately from service messaging, opt-outs apply across channels promptly, and birthdays or anniversaries are collected only when the guest chooses to share them. Profiles of inactive guests are deleted after an agreed period.

What we deliver

  • Unified guest profile with consent status
  • Segment definitions and campaign calendar
  • Approved template library
  • Return and opt-out reporting with holdout comparison

How we measure it

  • Repeat visit or booking rate
  • Lapsed guests returning after a campaign
  • Opt-out rate per campaign
  • Corporate event rebookings
